name: AL-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+23 partisan lean makes it deeply Republican territory
Rogers holds an overwhelming cash advantage ($2.6M on hand vs. $9.5K for McInnis)
Prediction markets price Rogers at roughly 98% to win
No polls or expert ratings exist; fundamentals carry the forecast
model.rationale: The R+23 district, Rogers' massive fundraising edge, and markets pricing him near 98% leave McInnis without a credible path, keeping the expected margin around 20 points Republican.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Rogers or a major scandal could tighten the race, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 3rd District is a heavily Republican seat, and incumbent Mike Rogers is seeking re-election with a large financial advantage. He has raised about $2.1 million and holds $2.6 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Lee McInnis has raised roughly $61,000 with under $10,000 available. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Rogers about a 98% chance of winning.

The district's partisan lean of roughly 23 points Republican, combined with Rogers' incumbency and fundraising edge, leaves McInnis with little visible path. The expected margin sits around 20 points Republican, with meaningful uncertainty because polling is absent. Barring an unforeseen development, Rogers is positioned for a comfortable win in November.
